title: SDK client surface evolution: semver-driven compatibility, deprecation policy, and cross-language adapters
creator: Emily Brooks
description: Product requirements and acceptance criteria for a coordinated SDK surface evolution across Python/TypeScript/Go. Goal: introduce a clear semantic versioning and deprecation policy, define a stable core API for text generation/paging/streaming/retries, and ship language-specific adapters that preserve backwards compatibility while enabling ergonomic new primitives (resumable streams, cursor-based pagination, idempotent retries). This ticket consolidates PRD clarifications, documents scope changes since the initial draft, and lists concrete acceptance criteria for engineering and DX teams.
scope_changes: Scope broadened from 'streaming semantics only' to full surface: pagination + retries + streaming + error model
Added language adapter requirement to avoid breaking existing idiomatic SDKs (Python iterator, TS async generator, Go channel-based stream)
Reduced initial breaking changes: move controversial cursor format change to a beta/adapter-only rollout
Introduced mandatory cross-language e2e tests and a migration guide as part of GA criteria
decisions: Adopt semantic versioning for all published SDKs. Any breaking change requires major version bump and documented migration guide.
Streaming stable core: define a minimal wire contract (chunk envelope with event types) but expose language idiomatic wrappers via adapters.
Pagination cursor contract: server-side opaque token; clients must treat cursor as opaque string. Optional expanded cursor schema will be offered via discovery API flagged as 'experimental'.

Retry policy: default client-side retry policy will be exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retries for idempotent endpoints; non-idempotent endpoints require explicit idempotency token to enable retries.
Backward compatibility mode: SDKs will ship compatibility helpers that translate new streaming envelopes into the legacy token stream for customers who opt-in.
Deprecation timeline: announce 90 days prior to breaking change; maintain legacy adapter support for one major version or 12 months, whichever is longer.
acceptance_criteria: API contract doc published: clear definitions for pagination cursor semantics, streaming envelope fields, retry idempotency rules, and error taxonomy.
Language adapters implemented and tested in Python/TypeScript/Go that present idiomatic surfaces: iterator/async-generator/channel respectively.
Automated cross-language e2e suite passes: pagination resume tests, streaming resume-on-network-glitch, and retry idempotency tests against staging runtime.
Migration guide and CHANGELOG entries for the release created and reviewed by Developer Experience and Security.
Rollback strategy documented: automatic fallback to legacy variant when the runtime returns compatibility flag or when adapter detects incompatible server response.
Performance benchmark: no more than 5% median-latency regression for common workloads when adapters are enabled versus existing SDKs.
Security review completed with KMS/identity implications documented for idempotency tokens and cursor handling.
open_questions: Should the expanded cursor schema be discoverable via a /capabilities endpoint or be entirely opt-in via a query param?
Do we require server-side guarantees for cursor monotonicity across model rollouts? (current plan: best-effort but document caveats)
How to instrument and surface upstream errors vs streaming end-of-sequence consistently across languages?
What migration incentives (feature flags, beta opt-in) do we offer to large customers with long-lived cursors?
